observations: A manual treadle sewing machine mounted in a wooden cabinet/table with folding top.
Machine head is cream/white with chrome knobs, visible paint chipping and black scuff marks on the body (photo 1, photo 2).
A brand badge on the front of the machine reads 'MERCURY' (photo 1, photo 2).
Cast iron treadle base with foot pedal grille marked 'SUPREME' is visible under the table (photo 0, photo 1, photo 2, photo 3).
Wooden cabinet is reddish-brown, shows general wear, scuffed edges and scratches on the folding lid (photo 2, photo 3).
No power cord or motor is visible; this appears to be a manual treadle-operated machine, not electric.
Photos are all taken outdoors in the same location with an advertising banner in the background; no close-up of stitching, bobbin area, or under-table mechanism.
No photo shows the machine threaded or in use, and no fabric sample stitched by it is shown.

claims.evidence: Photo 1 and photo 2 show chipped paint and dark scuff marks on the machine head, and photo 2/3 show wear on the wooden cabinet surface.

risks.risk: Internal stitching mechanism (tension, bobbin, needle feed) may not work smoothly
risks.proof: A short video clip of the machine being hand-cranked or treadled while stitching a scrap of fabric

risks.risk: Treadle belt could be missing, cracked, or slipping
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the belt loop connecting the wheel to the treadle mechanism

risks.risk: Rust or corrosion under the visible paint chips could affect moving parts
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the chipped areas and the underside metal frame
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic plus possible mechanical wear

risks.risk: Wooden cabinet joints/drawers may be loose or damaged, not clear from distance shots
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the drawer and the hinge of the folding lid
risks.if_unproven: priced as average cabinet condition, not premium

proof_requests: Video of the machine stitching a piece of cloth to confirm it works
Close-up photo of the belt and treadle linkage
Close-up photos of the chipped paint areas and the machine base for rust
Photo of the full open cabinet interior, drawers, and hinges
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a manual Mercury-brand treadle sewing machine in a wooden cabinet, but the seller's 'perfect condition' claim is contradicted by visible paint chipping and wear, so it must be priced at worst case pending proof of working stitching mechanism.
